is_anopheles.evidence: The study investigates Anopheles arabiensis (page 1, Abstract and Section 2.1 Study Area).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper does not genotype any target resistance markers; it only mentions in Section 2.2 that the insectary colony used 'exhibits established resistance mechanisms, including kdr mutations' without testing or specifying individual alleles.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No molecular genotyping was performed and no genotype counts, allele counts, or frequencies are presented in the study.

african_field_population.evidence: The study tested only an insectary-reared colony maintained since 2011 ('Third-instar larvae of pyrethroid-resistant An. arabiensis were obtained from the IHI insectary. This colony originated from field collections in Sakamaganga village, Ifakara, southern Tanzania, and has been maintained since 2011', Section 2.2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary experimental laboratory/semi-field study evaluating the effects of sublethal pyriproxyfen exposure across three generations.

sub_country_location.evidence: The semi-field experiments were conducted at Kinin'gina village (8.11417° S, 36.67484° E), rural southeastern Tanzania, and the colony originated from Sakamaganga village, Ifakara (page 3, Sections 2.1 and 2.2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Experiments were carried out between March and November 2024 (page 3, Section 2.1).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Original bioassay and life history data generated in a semi-field study using an established colony.

supplement.evidence: No external supplementary files are required as no molecular genotyping was conducted.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the multi-generational effects of sublethal pyriproxyfen exposure on fitness traits and pyrethroid susceptibility in a colonized strain of Anopheles arabiensis in Tanzania. It performed standard WHO tube bioassays and fitness assays, but did not perform any molecular marker genotyping.
exclusion_reasons: No target insecticide-resistance markers were genotyped.
No extractable genotype data (counts or frequencies) are reported.
Mosquitoes tested were strictly from a long-established laboratory insectary colony (maintained since 2011), rather than field-collected populations.
